lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs have stopped drifting and started pushing back. Thursday's 5-4 escape against the Rangers, sealed by Troy Stecher with 28 seconds left, made it three straight wins - a frantic victory, but a valuable one. Toronto is now 6-4, fourth in the Eastern Conference with 14 points, close enough to the leaders to matter and flawed enough to keep the alarm bell within reach. The cost is mounting: Chris Tanev, John Tavares, Nick Blankenburg and Marshall Rifai are all week-to-week, with Tavares staying home for the road trip. That leaves Toronto's blue line exposed just as Connor McDavid comes calling. Edmonton's Mattias Ekholm will miss the game with a concussion, but nobody should mistake that absence for relief. Tonight's visit to the Oilers at 7 p.m. ET is the measuring stick - can Toronto defend well enough to turn a hot streak into a credible climb?

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' offseason begins with an uncomfortable truth: a 79-83 team finishing second in the AL East still needs a serious overhaul. The season is over, and now the work moves from the field to the medical room and the front office. Ernie Clement serving as a World Series correspondent is a charming reminder of Toronto's place in the game, but the more consequential story is the return of injured players who could determine how aggressively the club shops for help. Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s post-operative update only sharpens that concern. Toronto cannot simply wait for better health, nor can it assume the offense will revive on its own. Louis Varland's emergence gives the bullpen a foundation, but the lineup and rotation require harder answers. Watch Toronto's first major move: a bat, a starter, or a medical green light that changes both.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors have opened the season by showing they can win ugly, and that matters more than a 43-point demolition of Chicago. Toronto's 112-102 victory over Washington on Friday made it 2-0, keeping the club atop the Atlantic Division and extending its winning streak to two. Scottie Barnes was the engine - 28 points and 14 rebounds - while RJ Barrett added 23 points and nine boards, and Kawhi Leonard chipped in 16. More telling: Toronto forced 23 turnovers and beat the Wizards with size, rebounding and second chances, the sort of grown-up basketball that travels. Nate Bittle is day-to-day with a foot issue, a small concern for a roster with only 14 players. Sunday's 7 p.m. visit to Minnesota is the first serious measuring stick: watch whether Barnes can impose this same physical edge against the Timberwolves.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The comeback offered a glimpse, but the loss exposed the larger fracture. Washington fell 23-17 to San Francisco and lost Terry McLaurin for the season to a torn patellar tendon - a cruel double blow in a game that demanded everything from Jayden Daniels. Daniels showed the Commanders what they have: fight, mobility and a quarterback capable of dragging a wounded offense back into a contest. He also showed what they lack. Washington remains 1-4-1, fourth in the NFC East and two games behind, with a one-game losing streak and precious little margin. The red zone has become the indictment: opponents have scored 18 touchdowns there, Washington nine. Now comes the bye, and then Philadelphia on November 1. That game will measure whether Daniels can build an offense without McLaurin - and whether Washington fixes the red-zone failures that keep turning winnable Sundays into losses.

article.title: Maple Leafs Visit Oilers in McDavid Test
paragraphs: The Leafs head to Edmonton tonight for a 7:00 PM ET meeting with the Oilers on Sportsnet, carrying a 6-4 record and fourth place in the Eastern Conference. Anthony Stolarz is projected to start against Tristan Jarry, with Stolarz at 3-1-0 and a 2.99 goals-against average. The Blue Jays are looking ahead, with the return of injured players set to shape Toronto's offseason plans.

The Raptors are 2-0 after beating the Wizards 112-102, led by Scottie Barnes' 28 points and 14 rebounds. Immanuel Quickley added six assists, and Toronto visits the Timberwolves Sunday at 7:00 PM ET. The Commanders are 1-4-1 and face the Eagles on November 1; receiver Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon. The Leafs-Oilers game begins at 7:00 PM ET.
